newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Bakun dam engineering pact signed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Bakun dam engineering pact signed.

text.p: Malaysia's Bakun Hydroelectric Corporation Bhd on Wednesday signed a $5.5 billion contract with a consortium led by ABB Asea Brown Boveri to build a hydroelectric dam in the Borneo state of Sarawak.
The deal was signed by Asea Brown Boveri and Brazil's Companhia Braseileira de Projectos e Obras (CBPO) on behalf of the consortium.
The signing was witnessed by Malaysia's Prime Minister, Mahathir Mohamad.
The deal was originally scheduled to be signed on Monday, but was delayed because of Ekran Bhd executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing's ill health.
Ekran is the dam's project manager.
Mahathir confirmed after the signing ceremony that Ting suffered a mild stroke recently.
"I think he had a mild problem, but that is not something to worry about," Mahathir told a news conference.
Asked if the problem was a mild stroke, Mahathir replied, "Yes, you can say it was a mild stroke."
Fears that Ting was ill had also roiled the share prices of Ekran and other Ting-controlled companies on Monday.
Construction of the 2,400 megawatt capacity project is expected to begin early in 1997 and be completed by 2002.

The dam project has been the target of environmental scrutiny and protests. It is to be built in the middle of tropical rainforests in Sarawak, submerging an area the size of Singapore, and displacing 9,400 tribal residents.
